cards.text: It's Pentecost in Jerusalem. The Holy Spirit just came on Jesus' followers, they're speaking languages they never learned, and some folks in the crowd are saying they're drunk. Then Peter, one of Jesus' apostles, stands up with the other eleven, lifts up his voice and tells the whole crowd to listen carefully.

cards.question: Peter tells the crowd these men are NOT drunk, the way people suppose, and he says that's because it's already late at night.

cards.text: It's only the third hour of the day! Friend, at that hour I'm still ARGUING with my snooze button. No, Peter says, this is what was spoken by Joel, one of God's prophets.

cards.question: In the words Peter quotes from Joel, who does God say He will pour out His Spirit on in the last days?

cards.text: It's ALL people: sons and daughters prophesy, young men see visions, old men dream dreams, and God pours out His Spirit even on menservants and maidservants. God is NOT checking anybody's job title at the door.

Then Joel's words turn to the sky: wonders in the heavens, signs on the earth, blood and fire and billows of smoke. The sun turned to darkness and the moon to blood, before the great and glorious Day of the Lord.

cards.question: After all those signs, Joel's words end with a promise: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be ___.

cards.text: Now Peter turns to the Man at the center of it all: Jesus of Nazareth. God certified Him with miracles, wonders and signs right among these people, and Peter says they know it themselves.

cards.question: Peter says Jesus was delivered up by a set plan and foreknowledge. Whose?

cards.text: And Peter doesn't tiptoe. He tells this crowd that they, by the hands of the lawless, put Jesus to death by nailing Him to the cross.

cards.question: Peter says God raised Jesus from the dead, because it was impossible for death to keep Him in its grip.

cards.text: Then Peter quotes David, Israel's king, and says David is talking about Jesus: ‘I saw the Lord always before me; because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.’

cards.question: David tells God He won't abandon David's soul to Hades or let His Holy One see decay. Because of that, how does David say his heart is?

cards.text: David's words end with joy in God's presence. Then Peter reminds them that David died and was buried, and his tomb is with them to this day.

cards.question: Peter says David was a prophet, and God had promised him on oath to put one of his descendants on his throne. So who was David really talking about?

answers.text: The Christ rising from the dead
His son Solomon on the throne

cards.question: Peter tells the crowd he's the only one who can vouch that God raised Jesus to life.
Peter says Jesus is exalted to the right hand of God and received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father. So the One who has poured out what the crowd now sees and hears is ___.

cards.text: David never ascended into heaven, Peter says. But David himself says: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”’

cards.question: Peter's big finish: let all Israel know with certainty that God has made this Jesus, whom they crucified, both ___ and ___.

cards.text: Peter's message LANDS. When the people hear this, they're cut to the heart.

cards.question: Cut to the heart, what does the crowd ask Peter and the other apostles?

answers.text: Brothers why did no one warn us

cards.question: Peter's answer is for every one of them. What two things does he tell them to do?
Peter tells them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of their ___.

cards.text: And they'll receive the gift of the Holy Spirit, the same Spirit this crowd just watched get poured out. Friend, that's not a free sample, that's the WHOLE cookie box.

cards.question: Peter says this promise belongs only to the people standing in front of him that day.

cards.text: It's for them, their children, and all who are far off, all whom the Lord our God will call. With many other words Peter keeps testifying, and he urges them, “Be saved from this corrupt generation.”

cards.question: Peter's message falls flat, and only a handful of people are baptized that day.

cards.text: Those who embraced his message were baptized, and about THREE THOUSAND were added to the believers that day. Friend, my biggest day welcoming newcomers to the junk drawer was a rubber band and a twist tie.

cards.question: The new believers devote themselves to the apostles' ___ and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to ___.

cards.text: A sense of awe comes over everyone, and the apostles perform many wonders and signs. All the believers are together and have everything in common.

cards.question: The believers sell their possessions and goods and share with anyone who is in need.

cards.text: With one accord they keep meeting daily in the temple courts, and they break bread from house to house, with gladness and sincerity of heart. Thousands of people with one accord, and I've watched a group chat of SIX fall apart over one emoji.

cards.question: They're praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And what does the Lord do, day after day?

answers.text: Adds to their number those being saved
Opens prison doors for the apostles
Gives them a new language to speak

findings.problem: The opening card gives context from outside the passage (Pentecost, the Spirit coming on the followers, the other languages, the crowd saying they're drunk). Those facts come from Acts 2:1-13, but the card cites only Acts 2:14 and never gives their reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with "Only the" and the right answer, "All people", is the only one without it. The right answer stands out by its form.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: "The sun turned to darkness and the moon to blood" puts Joel's future prophecy ("will be turned") in the past tense, so it reads as if it already happened.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Story card 12 says Peter "says David is talking about Jesus." That gives away the answer to card 15, which asks who David was really talking about (the Christ rising from the dead).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The right answer "Glad and full of hope" says David's heart is full of hope. Acts 2:26 says his heart is glad and his body will dwell in hope. The hope belongs to his body, not his heart.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: After the jokes on cards 3 and 5, Papa Dorin's voice disappears for the rest of the sermon. Story cards 8, 12, 14 and 18 are flat retellings with no reaction, comparison or storyteller energy. Some restraint fits the crucifixion moment on card 10, but the rest of the stop reads stripped down.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Story card 1 opens the stop with "Peter's message LANDS." That gives away the answer to the true or false on card 8 ("Peter's message falls flat...", which is False).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke makes a rubber band and a twist tie newcomers Papa Dorin welcomed to the drawer. In his backstory they were already in the drawer, and the first newcomer he welcomed was the can opener. This adds something new to his backstory.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "traditions" makes "the apostles' traditions," which is close in meaning to "the apostles' teaching." A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
